Chapter 6: Practical Value—Why Useful Information Travels Fast
Let’s dive into the next big idea: practical value.
At its heart, this principle is all about something deeply human—the urge we feel to help people by sharing useful information. Think about it: whenever you stumble on a clever tip, a great deal, or advice that saves time or money, don't you feel that itch to pass it along?
Sharing practical value isn’t just about being helpful—it's a way of showing you care, and it reinforces your reputation as someone others can count on.
Picture the last time you sent a friend a coupon, recommended a time-saving app, or shared a how-to video. Why did you do it? Chances are, you genuinely wanted to help. The more instantly useful or relevant something is, the harder it is to keep to yourself.
Practical value works because it solves a universal need: everyone’s looking for ways to make life easier, better, or just a bit less stressful. That’s why those “life hack” posts, honest product reviews, or step-by-step guides seem to pop up everywhere—they deliver real, tangible help, and people can’t wait to share them.
If you want practical value to catch on, focus on two things: clarity and specificity. Vague advice? It rarely goes far. People gravitate toward tips that are clear, concrete, and easy to act on. For example, a post called “5 Ways to Save $100 on Groceries This Month” is way more likely to get shared than just a generic article about budgeting.
Another piece of the puzzle is how shareable your information is. If a tip is simple to explain and quick to try out, people are far more likely to pass it along. Things like checklists, visuals, and short videos make practical value even stickier and easier to spread.
So, how do you boost practical value? Here are a few ideas:
First, highlight benefits that are clear and specific—don’t make anyone guess why it matters.
Second, package what you’re sharing in a way that’s easy to pass on, like with lists or visuals.
And third, aim for relevance—tailor your tips to the real needs and interests of your audience.
Imagine a hardware store running a campaign to help people winterize their homes. If they put together a simple checklist and a quick video showing how it’s done, homeowners are likely to share it with their neighbors and friends. It’s timely, super relevant, and easy to use.
Now, practical value doesn’t work in isolation. It gets even stronger when you mix it with other principles—like when useful information also boosts someone’s social currency, or it’s connected to a big seasonal event. For example, a tax-prep tip shared right before April? That’s both practical and perfectly timed, so it spreads even faster.
In the end, practical value is all about making lives better. When you help someone solve a problem or grab an opportunity, you create a positive ripple that encourages more sharing. It’s a powerful reminder: being genuinely helpful is often the best way to make your ideas, your products, and your message truly contagious.
